knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Empty tensor handling in dtype-specialized binary element-wise kernels
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Kernel implementations may assume non-empty buffers in dtype-specific code paths, leading to memory safety violations when an empty tensor is combined with a non-empty tensor.

risk_dimensions.shape: Empty or zero-element tensor shapes combined with non-empty tensors in broadcasting element-wise operations.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Half-precision and reduced-precision dtypes such as float16 and bfloat16, as well as dtype conversion paths that affect memory layout.
risk_dimensions.memory: Empty tensor storage characteristics, including zero-size buffers, null data pointers, and construction through array conversion versus direct allocation.
risk_dimensions.device: CPU backend dispatch and CPU-specific kernel assumptions; may also apply to other backends with specialized dtype kernels.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: No gradient tracking and element-wise binary operation execution, including operand ordering and broadcasting state.

failure_mechanism.description: CPU element-wise kernel incorrectly handles empty half-precision tensor inputs, potentially dereferencing invalid or empty storage because a dtype-specific path assumes a non-zero number of elements.

input_exploration: Explore empty, zero-element, scalar, and non-empty shape combinations for binary element-wise operations.
Vary dtypes around half precision including float16, bfloat16, float32, and integer types to isolate dtype-specific behavior.
Exercise multiple tensor construction paths for empty tensors, including direct allocation and array conversion.
Reverse operand order to test broadcasting and dispatch symmetry.
constraint_awareness: Keep execution on CPU to exercise CPU kernel implementations.
Disable gradient tracking to isolate forward kernel behavior.
Maintain the boundary of one empty and one non-empty tensor under the target dtype.
Respect broadcasting semantics when empty tensors participate.
oracle_strategy: Monitor process exit status and signals for hard crashes such as SIGSEGV or SIGBUS.
If the process survives, compare output shape and values against expected empty tensor broadcasting semantics.
Treat unexpected exceptions and nonzero exit codes as failures.

transferability.reason: The underlying principle is not specific to torch.mul: any element-wise binary kernel with dtype-specialized implementations may assume non-empty buffers when handling empty tensors, so APIs such as arithmetic, comparison, and logical operations share this risk across frameworks and backends.

important_considerations: Probe interactions between shape boundaries and dtype-specific kernel dispatch for element-wise binary operations.
Generate empty tensors through multiple construction paths, especially array-conversion and direct allocation.
Combine empty and non-empty tensors across dtypes and operand orders.
Include crash monitoring and semantic validation for empty tensor broadcasting.
generation_strategy: Use this knowledge to generate harnesses that systematically vary empty/non-empty shape combinations, dtype choices, construction paths, and operand order for binary element-wise APIs; avoid hardcoding the original float16/NumPy reproduction and instead explore the general class of empty tensor boundary conditions across related operations.
